subsystems.name: Isotopically purified silicon host
subsystems.role: the material the spins live in; removing silicon-29 nuclear spins greatly extends coherence.
parts: silicon-28 enriched wafer or Si/SiGe heterostructure

subsystems.name: Gate-defined quantum dots
subsystems.role: electrostatic cages that trap one or a few electrons each.
parts: tunnel barriers to an electron reservoir

subsystems.name: Spin control structures
subsystems.role: let the spin be rotated electrically rather than by a bulky microwave coil.
parts: micromagnet or stripline for a magnetic field gradient

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: senses whether a spin is up or down.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic environment
subsystems.role: keeps the device at millikelvin temperatures so the spins stay coherent.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: delivers precise nanosecond voltage pulses to many gates without cooking the fridge.

buildSteps.title: Enrich the silicon
buildSteps.detail: Natural silicon is about 5% silicon-29; isotopic separation raises the silicon-28 fraction above 99%, so far fewer nuclear spins disturb the qubits.

buildSteps.title: Grow the wafer stack
buildSteps.detail: On a silicon wafer, layers of silicon germanium and a thin strained silicon well are grown by epitaxy, or a gate oxide is grown for a silicon-MOS style device.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the gates
buildSteps.detail: Semiconductor lithography defines nanometre-scale metal gate electrodes; this is the step that could in principle run on existing CMOS production lines.

buildSteps.title: Cool and load electrons
buildSteps.detail: The chip is mounted in a dilution refrigerator at around 0.1 K, and gate voltages are tuned so single electrons tunnel in from a reservoir and are held in place.

buildSteps.title: Tune to the single-electron regime
buildSteps.detail: Automated tuning sweeps gate voltages until each dot holds exactly one electron and its charge state is stable.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate spin control and readout
buildSteps.detail: Microwave bursts on the gates flip spins; the sensor dot detects the resulting charge change, and gate fidelities are measured.

buildSteps.title: Build small arrays
buildSteps.detail: Two, four or more dots are coupled in a line or grid so neighbouring spins can interact for two-qubit gates.

buildSteps.title: Multiplex the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Cryogenic control chips and crossbar addressing reduce the number of wires running from room temperature, which is the main obstacle to larger arrays.

buildSteps.title: Operate error-corrected logical qubits
buildSteps.detail: Many physical spins are combined into one protected logical qubit — a milestone not yet reached in silicon.

prerequisites.why: the key promise is that these qubits are made with the same lithography, oxides and metal gates as ordinary microchips.
it is produced in small quantities at high cost; large, uniform wafers would be needed for manufacturing.
dilution refrigerators are standard laboratory equipment, but each one supports only a limited number of qubits and wires.
cryo-CMOS multiplexers have been demonstrated at a few kelvin, but addressing thousands of gates is unsolved.
no platform, including silicon, has yet run enough qubits with low enough error rates to make a reliably protected logical qubit.

pathway.milestone: laboratory devices with a handful of spins; single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.9% in purified silicon
pathway.unlocks: confidence that spins are a viable qubit, and that some devices work near 1 K.

pathway.milestone: tens to hundreds of qubits with integrated cryogenic control and automated tuning
pathway.unlocks: system-level tests of wiring, calibration and reliability on a chip.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrated error-corrected logical qubit in silicon
pathway.unlocks: the first credible route to scaling by adding more dots rather than more fridges.

pathway.milestone: fab-compatible production of many-qubit chips, with modules linked by spin shuttling or microwave cavities
pathway.unlocks: large quantum processors built on existing semiconductor supply chains.
